mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.5 percentage points over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 3% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence, or the trigger does not precede a decline in earnings revisions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month MA, or the joint trigger does not precede a decline in equity valuations as measured by Shiller CAPE.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the previous 12-month average for four consecutive months signals a weakening residential construction sector, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the trigger does not coincide with a decline in related sector ETFs.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification, which historically coincides with short-term equity volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both move by > 0.3% in the same month (opposite directions)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede abnormal volatility as measured by realized volatility.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which depresses demand for consumer discretionary goods and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a decline in consumer discretionary sector performance.
